requirements.requirement: Every sudo command run on node1 is recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: A sudoers.d drop-in (/etc/sudoers.d/sudo-commands-log) sets Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log" and log_year, validated with visudo -c/-cf. Captured log content shows entries in the form 'Sep 29 10:20:30 2026 : root : PWD=... ; USER=root ; COMMAND=...', directly demonstrating user and full timestamp are recorded for each invocation, including a post-reboot invocation (sudo whoami).

requirements.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log (journald/secure)
requirements.summary: After adding Defaults !syslog, journal SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER=sudo and /var/log/secure COMMAND= counts both stayed frozen at 7 pre-existing entries while a new command (ls -la /) produced zero new COMMAND= lines in secure/journal but did appear in the dedicated log. This directly compares before/after behavior rather than relying only on configuration.

overall_summary: The executor created /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-commands-log with logfile, log_year, and !syslog directives, validated it, and directly demonstrated via before/after command counts that sudo invocations are now recorded (user, full timestamp, PWD, COMMAND) in /var/log/sudo-commands.log and excluded from /var/log/secure and journald. Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct observational evidence, not just configuration inspection.
limitations: The additional provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol (not required by the task itself) was executed reasonably completely: pre-restart boot_id and healthy state (cmd-815dcc79ff7548d9), restart acknowledgement (cmd-cb91c0cbac844840), differing post-restart boot_id (cmd-46c63bf34a9544ce, corroborated by the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot), and recovered config/log functionality (cmd-21dbdce36071474f) were all captured, though the reboot mechanism left a minor /tmp/reboot.log residue.

Persistence of the sudoers.d config across reboot was verified only by file presence and visudo -c after a single restart cycle; longer-term persistence (e.g., across package updates) was not tested, though this exceeds what the task required.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary or destructive mutations were found. The sudoers.d file creation is the sole persistent mutation and it directly serves the task requirement. The reboot (cmd-cb91c0cbac844840) was a bounded, single-node, non-task-required action performed solely to gather the provider-wide restart evidence protocol; it left a small residue file /tmp/reboot.log (nohup output redirect) visible in the after-executor snapshot, a minor and low-risk leftover rather than a substantive residue. All other executed commands were read-only diagnostics (os-release, sudo -l, journalctl counts, file listings, boot_id checks) with no state-changing side effects beyond the sudo invocations' own logging, which is expected and intended by the task.
